description: P6 (D-153) source rows for the demand system, saving and housing of the 1900 world. Authored transcriptions read from page images (or a text layer where noted); every value has its locator and status. Read by scripts/p5b/build-goods-1900.mjs (P6 stage, scripts/p6/demand.mjs); docs/P6_DEMAND_PROVENANCE.md is generated from it.

budget1901ByIncome.note: Each row's five non-food items sum to the printed total of preceding; the family counts sum to 11,156. The 'total of all' column is cut by the binding of the scan and is computed as preceding + food.

childrenByIncome1901.locator: Table V-L, pp. 582-583 (PDF 725-726): normal families by number of children and classified income
childrenByIncome1901.note: Rows: 0 to 5 children; columns: the twelve income classes of budget1901ByIncome. Each column sums to that class's family count. A normal family is husband, wife and up to five children; average size 3.96 persons (text p. 92, PDF 93).

childFactor.note: Atwater factor of a child of unknown age in a 1901 normal family (children 0-15; the bulletin's factors run from 0.3 to 0.9).

surplus1901.locator: text p. 96 (PDF 97): the 11,156 normal families spent 94.90 per cent of income, leaving a surplus of 5.10 per cent

retailQuantities1901.locator: p. 165 (PDF 171): average quantity per family of certain principal articles of food consumed in 1901, United States, 2,567 families
retailQuantities1901.note: Retail price paid = the article's share of food spending (foodArticles1901 of the P5b sources, parts of 10,000) x 326.90 USD / quantity.

engel1853.locator: Table 2, p. 39 (PDF 51): Mark per Quet per year; Table 4, p. 40 (PDF 54): per cent of expenditure I-XII

quetsPerAdultEquivalent.note: Engel's Quet: a newborn is 1, an adult man 3.5; taken as one Atwater adult equivalent (man at moderate work).

usdPerMark.note: gold parity, Director of the Mint, Values of Foreign Coins (4.198 Mark per dollar)

cpi1853Over1900.note: US consumer prices of 1853 and 1900 were about equal (Minneapolis Fed series); a precise 1853 Belgian deflator is not used.

cex1990.unit: USD per consumer unit per year

adultEquivalentsPerConsumerUnit.note: average consumer unit of 2.6 persons in 1990 on Atwater's scale; size by quintile not transcribed

cex1990.note: Quintile categories sum to total expenditures (checked for q1 and q5). Shelter is excluded from consumption (housing is owner-occupied in P6) and personal insurance and pensions (mostly Social Security) are treated as saving.

housing1900.note: Persons per dwelling (inhabited house) at the census nearest 1900, by modern country of the P4 crosswalk; countries without a census figure take the median of the sourced values.

usa.locator: p. 303: dwellings 1900 14,430,000, 5.3 persons per dwelling (US census definition)

gbr.locator: p. 301: UK 1901 inhabited houses 8,045,924 (England and Wales 6,260,852 at 5.20 persons; Scotland 926,914; Ireland 858,158); UK population 41.46 M

irl.locator: p. 301: Ireland 1901 inhabited houses 858,158 for 4,458,775 persons

ind.locator: p. 304: India 1901 occupied houses 55,841,300, 5.3 persons per house (British territory 5.3, native states 5.0)

nld.locator: p. 302: Netherlands 1899, 5.73 persons per inhabited house

fra.locator: p. 302: France 1901 occupied dwelling-houses 7,006,133 for 38,961,945 persons

can.locator: p. 303: Canada 1901 houses 1,068,951 (incl. vacant and building) for 5,371,315 persons

aus.locator: p. 303: Australia 1901 inhabited dwellings 745,176 for 3,773,801 persons

nzl.locator: p. 303: New Zealand 1886, 5.17 persons per inhabited dwelling (1906: 4.82)

deu.locator: p. 302: German households 1900 12,260,000 for 56.37 M persons (no house count; households taken as dwellings)

defaultValue.note: median of the sourced country values

dwellingCost1900.locator: series N 167, average construction cost per new non-farm housing unit started, 1900 (p. 640, PDF 31)

dwellingRecipe.note: Materials of one standard dwelling (a frame-and-brick workman's house of four to five rooms): about 40 m3 of lumber (17,000 board feet), 25 t of brick, lime, cement and plaster, 0.4 t of nails, hardware and pipe, 0.1 t of paint and glass. The rest of the price is building labour and the builder's margin (D-135 A3 sizing).

dwellingIncomeElasticity.note: elasticity = ln(5.3 / 2.63) / ln(36982 / 8037.57) = 0.46; the 1990 persons per occupied unit is to be confirmed from the 1992 Statistical Abstract.

tastes1901.locator: Commerce article: annual consumption per head of population of wheat, rye, sugar, tea and coffee in several countries, data mainly of 1901
tastes1901.status: sourced (text layer; two OCR readings marked)
tastes1901.note: Used as national tastes (plan Q16): the weight of coffee-tea-cocoa and of sugar in a country's food category relative to the United States, by the value of tea and coffee (at 1901 US retail prices) and of sugar per head. Countries not listed take no taste multiplier.
